conviction_note: The quarter itself is guided and the consensus sits at the midpoint, so the move turns on the Q4 guide and on 2027 commentary. A Guggenheim channel check (gaming client ramp-down, Middle East, Q4 exit flat y/y) and Disney's new $3B cost programme point to a Q4 guide at or below the street's $611.2M. Against that, the stock is down 12% in five sessions to $40.26 into the print, about 25% of shares are short at 10.7 days to cover, and the option market pays 38 vol points more for calls than for puts. That leaves a near-balanced p_up of 53 on a 13% absolute move. impact_sum is +2.1 because the positioning findings are sized on their own. The scaled +0.78 is smaller because the guide-cut history (-9 to -24% on each cut) keeps p_up close to 50.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-11 Guggenheim (Jonathan Lee) downgraded GLOB to Neutral and pulled its $50 target. It cited weak bookings, softer Middle East demand, a possible ramp-down at a large gaming client, a Q4 2026 exit rate roughly flat y/y, a possible sequential revenue decline into Q1 2027 and a flat 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 5.6% on the day of the note. On Q3'25 the Q4 guide came in below consensus ($605M against $607M) and the stock fell about 9% intraday and 2.8% at the close.
findings.why_not_priced: The note itself is priced, since the stock fell 5.6% that day. What is not priced is the client-level confirmation: the street's Q4 at $611.2M still sits at the implied guide midpoint and has not moved to the 'flat exit' and 'ramp-down' view. If it had, the Q4 consensus would sit below $605M.
findings.independence: Fool.com coverage of the same note: https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/11/11/why-globant-stock-wilted-by-5-on-wednesday/ (same document, counts once). The Disney finding below is a different source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The Q4 guide is the deciding line. The FY26 guide ($2,428-2,462M) less H1 actual ($1,221.5M) less the Q3 guide ($607-615M) implies Q4 of about $591-634M, midpoint about $612.5M, which equals Q4 2025's $612.5M (flat y/y). The street's Q4 is $611.2M, so it already sits at the midpoint. Any trim of the FY range, or a Q4 guide under about $605M, would be a below-street guide. GLOB has cut or under-guided at 4 of its last 6 prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide line has driven every large move: Q1'25 cut -23.6, Q2'25 cut -14.9, Q3'25 light Q4 guide -2.8 (about -9 intraday), Q2'26 cut -8.8. Q1'26 held the midpoint while raising the low end: +14.2.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 still sits at the guide midpoint (Benzinga $611.2M) even though channel checks (Guggenheim) and the largest client (Disney) point to the low half. A priced cut would show a Q4 consensus near $600M.
findings.independence: Q4 2025 revenue of $612.5M comes from the 2026-02-26 release (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/453321/globant-reports-2025-fourth-quarter-financial-results), a different document. The Guggenheim 'flat Q4 exit' view is a separate source that agrees with the arithmetic.

findings.finding: Disney, Globant's largest client (8.7% of 2024 revenue per the 20-F; top customer 8.9% of Q2 2026 revenue), reported on 2026-11-17 before the open. It set an annual savings target of about $3B by FY2029, said further savings will come from administrative and general expense, and its CFO said 'we do expect more layoffs'. It had cut hundreds of technology roles in September. GLOB fell 6.8% intraday the same day. Against that, Disney guides FY27 content spend up 9% to about $26B.
findings.link: Disney is Globant's largest client: 8.7% of revenue in 2023 and 2024 (20-F FY2024, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1557860/000162828025009110/glob-20241231.htm); top customer 8.9% in Q2 2026 (6-K); BA Times says nearly 10%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned explicitly on Disney. The 2026-11-17 intraday -6.8% is this name's reaction to the Disney headline itself.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced already (the -6.8% move). What remains open is whether Globant's 2027 commentary or Q4 guide names top-client budget pressure. Net of the rest of the company it is small: about 9% of revenue, and Disney's content and streaming spend is growing.
findings.independence: https://www.ajc.com/news/2026/11/disney-theme-parks-and-streaming-services-thrive-as-new-ceo-seeks-3-billion-in-cost-savings/ is a separate outlet on the same Disney release, so it counts once.

Guggenheim's 'large gaming client ramp-down' fits this, but no source found names EA as a Globant client or its revenue share.

findings.finding: EPAM reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05 and beat. Revenue was $1.426B (+2.3% y/y) and non-GAAP EPS $3.51. findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: GLOB's +14.2% on Q1'26 came on AI-native momentum, the same theme EPAM was rewarded for.
findings.why_not_priced: GLOB has fallen since EPAM's print while EPAM rallied, so the read-across has not carried into GLOB. If it had, GLOB would have held $45-46. The read is mixed, though: EPAM's own Q4 is also flat and its Americas region is weak.

findings.finding: Saudi Arabia froze consulting spend and work on existing contracts at ministries and PIF subsidiaries in May 2026. Globant's 'new markets' (Asia, Oceania, Middle East) fell about 18% in Q2, and about half of the August guide cut was attributed to new markets. Management said the guide assumes Saudi weakness persists.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 guide cut, about half attributed to new markets: -8.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced and inside the current guide. It is only incremental if Q4 needs a further new-markets cut, which Guggenheim's 'softer Middle East' hints at.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview: new markets -18% in Q2, management assumes Saudi weakness persists (https://finviz.com/news/421349/globants-ai-pods-must-outrun-a-shrinking-core-after-a-guidance-cut-and-restructuring).

findings.finding: The Colombian peso, a major Globant delivery-cost currency, appreciated against the dollar in Q3 2026 and outperformed regional peers until early September (BanRep). That pressures the Q3 adj. margin, which is guided at 13.5-14.5% after Q2's 13.2% missed the range partly on FX. The peso reversed sharply in the last two weeks of September after a Fed hike, which helps Q4 cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 margin miss (13.2% against the range), with FX cited: -8.8%, which also included the guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-margin transmission is unconfirmed by the company, so this is a small proxy. The Q3 guide was set in mid-August with the peso already strong.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Earnings Whispers notes management expects a multi-year headwind from LatAm currency strength, especially the Colombian peso (same preview as other findings).

findings.finding: Glob.AI ARR was $52.8M at June 2026, up 61% q/q from $32.8M. Management guided at least $110M exiting 2026 (raised from $60-100M), with a $436.8M pipeline and adoption in more than 45% of top-20 accounts. It said AI-pod revenue was about 2% of total and expected about 4% by year-end, and on 2026-10-27 launched Glob.AI OS. The Q3 ARR disclosure needs to land around $75-85M to look on-track.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1'26: AI-pod ARR and adoption momentum with a held guide gave +14.2%. Q2'26: ARR +61% did not offset the cut (-8.8%).
findings.why_not_priced: No interim ARR has been published since June. Guggenheim stays positive on AI pods while downgrading, so the line is not in the bear case. An ARR print near $80M would be new information. It is two-sided: a miss on the doubling path would remove the bull case.
findings.independence: BA Times 2026-10-01: Migoya expects the AI business at 4-6% of revenue by year-end (https://batimes.com.ar/news/economy/globant-goes-all-in-on-ai-overhaul-to-rebuild-from-80-sell-off.phtml).

findings.finding: Globant had $125.0M left on its buyback authorization at 2026-06-30, about 7% of a market cap near $1.74B at $40.26 times 43.2M diluted shares. Migoya has called buybacks one of the highest-return uses of capital (2026-10-01), and the CFO expected stronger H2 free cash flow. Cash and short-term investments were $168.8M, and Q2 FCF was $12.6M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25: a buyback was announced alongside a light guide and the stock fell 2.8% at the close. Peer EPAM's $500M ASR was rewarded on 2026-11-05.
findings.why_not_priced: Any upsizing would be new. The limited cash ($168.8M) caps it, so this is small.
findings.independence: BA Times 2026-10-01 on Migoya and buybacks (https://batimes.com.ar/news/economy/globant-goes-all-in-on-ai-overhaul-to-rebuild-from-80-sell-off.phtml).

findings.finding: Globant flagged a further $20-25M business-optimization charge for Q3 after $32.3M in Q2. It is excluded from non-IFRS operating profit, so IFRS EPS will be low.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2'26 carried $32.3M; the move was driven by the guide, not the charge.
findings.why_not_priced: It is flagged and inside the guidance framework. It only matters if the charge or headcount cuts are extended into 2027.
findings.independence: Q2 6-K: business optimization costs of $32.3M, programme begun April 2026 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001557860/000110465926095916/tm2623064d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: The Q3 2026 release is on 2026-11-19, six days later in the calendar than Q3 2025 (2025-11-13). Earlier aggregator estimates had 2026-11-12. The date was announced on 2026-11-05.
findings.why_not_priced: Weak signal, and it may simply be calendar logistics. Sized near zero.

findings.finding: Globant has met or beaten its revenue bar on four straight prints: Q3'25 $617.1M against $615.3M, Q4'25 $612.5M about $7M above, Q1'26 $607.1M against $601.7M, Q2'26 $614.4M inside the guide and above the street. Against the $611.1M consensus and the $607-615M guide, a small revenue beat is the base case. The EPS whisper ($1.52) sits above the consensus ($1.47).

findings.why_not_priced: A beat is the base case and mostly priced. The whisper sits above consensus, so a mid-guide EPS print reads as a miss to the buy side.

findings.finding: Insiders sold about 14,500 shares (about $585k) over the past 90 days and own about 2.67%.
